products.name: Soundraw
products.note: Royalty-free AI music; commercial license; JASRAC considerations for Japan use

reading.body:
Soundraw, founded in 2020 and based in Tokyo, generates royalty-free music using AI trained only on its own in-house producer catalog, giving users worldwide commercial licenses with no royalty splits.

The company's core legal claim distinguishes it from generative AI tools that train on scraped internet data. By training exclusively on owned recordings and compositions, Soundraw positions itself as avoiding the copyright litigation that has plagued other generative music platforms. Users receive perpetual commercial rights to generated tracks, keeping all royalties—a straightforward licensing model that reduces friction for commercial deployment.

This approach trades breadth for legal clarity. A model trained on a controlled internal catalog will generate music within narrower stylistic bounds than one trained on millions of songs. The tradeoff works if users value legal certainty and commercial viability over maximum creative range. The platform's bar-level editing and stem export suggest it targets music creators who want AI assistance within professional workflows, not casual beat-making.

The data does not reveal how large Soundraw's training catalog is, what computing infrastructure supports generation, or how its model scales with user demand. The reference to JASRAC considerations indicates the company operates in regulated music licensing environments and must navigate different rules by jurisdiction. The company's self-description as responsible and its association with the aiformusic initiative suggest positioning around industry legitimacy, but the data does not show whether this affects its technical development or cost structure.
